description: Create AI skincare and makeup ads from product photos. Explore GRWM, texture demos, creator reviews, shade swatches, and unboxings for short social placements.
h1: Beauty UGC Ads for Skincare and Makeup
lead: Turn a clear product photo into a short ad concept that shows a serum, lipstick, or skincare set in use. Choose a routine, shade or texture demo, creator review, or unboxing.
card: Short beauty ad formats for creator reviews, shade demos, routines, and unboxings.
intro: A hand demo can show how a product is applied, and a swatch can put a shade beside its tube. Keep ingredient and result claims consistent with approved product details.
Use GRWM, creator-review, unboxing, and hand-demo formats for short feed ads. Upload a clear photo of the item you want to show, then review packaging, shade, and label details before publishing.

ideas.d: Show one clear step, such as applying a balm before makeup or patting a serum into the skin. A vertical frame suits short-form placements.
Use a close view of a cream, lipstick, or swatch so shoppers can see the finish. Check color against a real sample before publishing.
An adult creator can introduce the product in their own words, or hands can open a set and reveal its contents.

faq.q: Can I make before-and-after videos for a skincare product?
faq.a: We’d steer away from it for skin results. A generated face is not evidence of what your product does, and a visible change in skin can read as a promise. Show application, texture, and packaging instead, and leave claims about results out of your request and the claims you use in an ad.

faq.q: Will the video match my exact foundation or lipstick shade?
faq.a: Color comes from your photo and your wording, so shoot in daylight and name the shade plainly, like "warm beige liquid" or "brick red matte." If the tone still drifts, generate another version; the credit cost is shown before each one.

faq.q: Can I add my price or a promo code to the image?
faq.a: Type prices, promo codes, and product names on afterward in Canva or CapCut. Lettering made by AI can come out misspelled, so keep the image clean and add the words yourself.

faq.q: What kind of product photo should I upload for skincare?
faq.a: A straight-on shot with the label toward the camera, on a plain surface, with no hands or clutter in the frame. Glossy tubes and clear glass pick up glare, so shoot beside a window rather than using flash.

overview.h2: Show what the product looks like in use

items.t: Put texture, shade, and packaging in focus
items.d: A close view can show a lipstick swatch, cream texture, or serum applicator. Keep ingredient and shade claims in approved product details.

items.t: Build each short ad around one action
items.d: Show a routine step, open a set, or let an adult creator discuss the item. Review the package and any visible product details before you publish.
Place the bottle, tube, or jar upright with the front label toward the camera. Include the full cap and base so the package shape is not guessed.
Use a window or diffused lamp beside the product instead of direct flash. Rotate glossy plastic and clear glass until the label is readable and hot spots are small.
For a cream, balm, powder, or lipstick, add a separate swatch or texture photo. A packshot cannot reveal a finish that never appears in the upload.
Lay out all bottles, minis, pouches, or tools for a bundle shot. Keep the pieces separated enough that the final count is easy to check.

items.t: Keep claims out of the scene
items.d: Describe a bathroom shelf, mirror tray, or travel pouch rather than an implied medical outcome. Add approved claims later in the channel where your team controls the wording.

after_download.h2: Finish the beauty asset after download

items.d: Compare cap shape, label placement, shade, and item count with the real package before publishing.
Place price, shade name, promotion dates, and approved claims in Canva, CapCut, or your ad editor so every character is exact.
AIVideosUGC does not add voiceover, music, or captions; add shade names and product details in your publishing tool after download.

fit.h2: A good fit for beauty products

good.d: Bottles, jars, tubes, compacts, and boxed sets with a clear front view.
Creams, powders, balms, drops, and swatches that you can photograph separately.
Products that benefit from a shelf, vanity, travel, or gift-set context.

not_ideal.d: Do not use a generated image as the sole proof of a precise color match; compare with a real swatch.
